# Saloni Garg - Full Public Profile

> Saloni Garg - GPU optimization, RLHF, and multimodal inference engineering. Staff Machine Learning Engineer at Adobe Firefly, San Jose, CA.

Source: https://saloni-garg.github.io/
Last updated: 2026-11-06
Contact: salonigarg2318@gmail.com | LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/saloni-garg

## Summary

Saloni Garg is a Staff Machine Learning Engineer at Adobe (Firefly) in San Jose, CA. Her primary positioning is GPU optimization, RLHF, and multimodal inference engineering.

She leads development of the post-training and RLHF pipelines for multimodal foundation models, supporting SFT, DPO, and reward model training, along with distributed GPU training and automated evaluation infrastructure at scale. She optimizes GPU training and inference for multimodal models in production, including video diffusion inference.

She previously worked at Wayfair as a Senior ML Infrastructure Engineer in Mountain View, CA, and before that as a Founding ML Engineer at Brisko in Bengaluru, India. She is recipient of the 2026 CITRIS Award by UC Berkeley.

Focus: GPU optimization (CUDA, Triton, kernel profiling, GPU utilization) / RLHF and post-training (SFT, DPO, RLVR, GRPO, reward models) / multimodal inference engineering (TensorRT, Dynamo, vLLM, SGLang, dynamic batching, latency and throughput) / distributed GPU training (PyTorch, FSDP, NCCL) / evaluation infrastructure.

## Experience

### Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Adobe (Firefly) - Jul 2025 to Present, San Jose, CA

- Led development of the post-training and RLHF pipelines for multimodal foundation models, supporting SFT, DPO, and reward model training, with distributed GPU training using PyTorch, CUDA, FSDP, and NCCL.
- Built distributed training and evaluation infrastructure for large-scale model iteration, model quality, reasoning, and safety.
- Built RLHF preference data generation and curation pipelines for post-training and alignment.
- Partnered with research scientists to productionize post-training algorithms for multimodal models up to 80B parameters, enabling reproducible large-scale experimentation and regular model releases.
- Optimized video diffusion inference by profiling UNet, attention, VAE, and temporal modules, and by improving GPU execution, batching, and request scheduling for video generation workloads, including KV cache optimization, speculative decoding, and prefill-decode disaggregation; quantized diffusion-based models for production inference.
- Built and served multilingual generation models in production, including speech and audio generation, translation, and lip syncing.
- Note: Detailed employer metrics on the homepage are the site presentation as published by Saloni Garg. No salary, visa, or private employer data is included in this file.

### Senior ML Infrastructure Engineer, Wayfair - Oct 2020 to Jul 2025, Mountain View, CA

- Productized ML systems for search and recommendation, and optimized distributed model-serving pipelines for latency and throughput.
- Developed high-throughput Python and C++ inference and feature-processing components.
- Designed scalable offline and online inference pipelines and distributed benchmarking and performance-analysis tooling.

### Founding ML Engineer, Brisko - Jul 2017 to Oct 2020, Bengaluru, India

- Built the core voice AI and NLP stack from scratch: speech-to-text, intent classification, entity extraction, and dialogue understanding.
- Developed and optimized real-time voice inference pipelines for conversational assistants.

### Education

- B.Tech, Computer Science and Engineering, The LNM Institute of Information Technology, Jaipur, India (LNMIIT).

## Selected Work

- Memline (2026): Trustworthy memory layer for AI applications: a grounding write gate that rejects memories the source does not support, temporal validity with full revision history, explainable retrieval, and Memory Health reporting. Ships a /v1 REST API, Python and TypeScript SDKs, an MCP server, and a migration and audit tool for existing memory stores. Apache 2.0. https://github.com/saloni-garg/memline
- AgentLab (2026): A reproducible laboratory for studying the scaling behavior of LLM agent organizations. Config-driven experiments, calibration gates, deterministic replay, and sealed, auditable results. Version 1.0 released publicly. https://saloni-garg.github.io/agentlab.html
- gpu-train-debug (2026): RL environment for diagnosing GPU training failures, in Prime Intellect Verifiers format. Published on the Prime Intellect Hub and as a dataset on Hugging Face. https://huggingface.co/datasets/sluuu/gpu-train-debug
- memfix (2026): Provenance-first, correctable memory layer for AI agents: source pointers, append-only log, tombstones, and an MCP server. MIT. https://github.com/saloni-garg/memfix
- jev-max (2026): Browser agent for general web tasks: shadow DOM and iframe handling, canvas vision fallback, uploads, drag and drop, multi-tab support, MCP server, and a benchmark suite. MIT. https://github.com/saloni-garg/jev-max

## Open Source Contributions

Contributor to Ray and PyTorch. Recent upstream pull requests include:

- GRPO uniform-reward group fix, sent to five codebases: verl, slime, OpenRLHF, SkyRL, EasyR1. When every response in a GRPO group earns the same reward, the advantage should be exactly zero; float32 group statistics invented a nonzero advantage instead. All five pull requests open as of November 2026.
- Triton interpreter: fix for NaN and Inf handling in float conversions. Merged into triton-lang/triton on 30 October 2026 (PR #12489).
- torch_tpu: two fixes for view decomposition, both landed on main via Copybara (PR #5847 on 29 October 2026, commit 5731cd51; PR #5846 on 30 October 2026, commit dbdccfaf). GitHub shows these PRs as closed with merged=false because Copybara closes the PR when it imports the change to main. Closed here means landed, not rejected.
- AllenAI open-instruct: fix for the R1-style format reward gate, which compared scores against a literal 1 instead of the configured reward scale (PR #2134, open).
- AllenAI open-instruct: fix for local dataset directory caches, which were keyed on the directory path alone, so rewriting shards in place silently trained on stale rows; the cache is now keyed on a hash of the directory contents (PR #2159, open).
- SkyRL: fix for the arctic_rl BIRD reward cap, which was skipped whenever the text LIMIT appeared anywhere in the query; only a top level LIMIT clause now suppresses the cap (PR #2603, open).
- OpenEnv: fix to stop code verifiers from passing on an untouched database.
- OpenAI human-eval: fix so a completion ending in a decorator cannot replace the test check function.
- Anthropic jacobian-lens: raise on save when the storage dtype would turn finite entries into infinity.
- NVIDIA Dynamo: profiler fix for SGLang multinode placement spellings.
- NVIDIA Dynamo: admission validation fix, so disaggregated serving configs whose backend framework cannot be resolved are rejected at admission, including mixed worker frameworks across a graph (PR #17801, open).
- SGLang: detokenizer worker processing time histogram (sglang:detokenizer_processing_seconds), one slice of the metric coverage umbrella in issue #43304 (PR #47877, open).
- NVIDIA Model-Optimizer: fix for static NVFP4 fake quantization in TensorQuantizer, routed through the static blockwise fake quant path instead of raising NotImplementedError (PR #3167, open).

Full list: https://saloni-garg.github.io/#oss
